'''John Riley''' (born 23 April 1958) is an Australian scientist at the [[Defence Science and Technology Group|Defence Science and Technology Organisation]] and former [[Australian rules football]]er who played with [[Footscray Football Club|Footscray]] in the [[Victorian Football League (1897–1989)|Victorian Football League]] (VFL) and [[North Adelaide Football Club|North Adelaide]] in the [[South Australian National Football League]] (SANFL).<ref name="Malthouse">{{cite web |url=http://www.afl.com.au/news/2015-05-01/the-man-mick-almost-coached |title=The man Mick almost coached: the story of John Riley |last=Ryan |first=Peter |publisher=Telstra Media |website=AFL.com.au |date=1 May 2015 |accessdate=25 June 2015}}</ref>

==Scientist==
Riley played football for [[North Adelaide Football Club]] while he was studying at [[Flinders University]]. He was still finishing off his [[PhD]] in [[atomic physics]] when he was recruited to the [[Western Bulldogs|Footscray Football Club]] in the [[Victorian Football League (1897–1989)|Victorian Football League]] (VFL). He returned to Adelaide after only playing one match for Footscray.<ref name="Malthouse"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Turner |first1=Matt |title=One-game Wonders: Ex-North Adelaide captain John Riley recalls court injunction stopping him from playing more games at Footscray |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/afl/local-footy-sa/onegame-wonders-exnorth-adelaide-captain-john-riley-recalls-court-injunction-stopping-him-from-playing-more-games-at-footscray/news-story/a33a40a09ba40e23f6e1b20bf02a49b7 |accessdate=26 September 2019 |work=adelaidenow.com.au |date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

Riley completed an Australian Research Grants Scheme research fellowship, then worked in the development of instrumentation for the mining industry.<ref name="DSTO"/>

Riley moved to the [[Defence Science and Technology Group|Defence Science and Technology Organisation]] (DSTO), the research arm of the Australian Department of Defence, in 1988, initially working on [[sonar]] [[signal processing]] which improved the performance of [[towed array]] and [[sonobuoy]] systems.<ref name="DSTO">{{cite web |url=http://www.dsto.defence.gov.au/staff/dr-john-riley |title=Dr John Riley |publisher=Defence Science and Technology Organisation |year=2015 |accessdate=25 June 2015}}</ref>

Riley was awarded a Defence Science Fellowship in 1993, leading to two-year at the [[Defence Research Establishment Atlantic]] in Nova Scotia, Canada, and subsequently to the Aeronautical and Maritime Research Laboratory Best Research Award in 1996.<ref name="DSTO"/> Riley worked as the Navy Scientific Adviser in 1997, and then was appointed as head of Airborne Sonar leading a research programme in support of the [[RAAF]] [[Lockheed P-3 Orion|P3-C Orion]] maritime patrol aircraft and [[Royal Australian Navy|RAN]] [[Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk|Seahawk]] helicopters.<ref name="DSTO"/>

Riley spent a year based in Washington, D.C. as Defence Science Attaché supporting liaison between Australia, the US and Canada. He then returned to Australia to lead submarine operations research for DSTO, based at {{HMAS|Stirling}} in Western Australia. This included improvements to the ''Collins''-class combat and sonar systems. Afterwards, he moved to Research Leader of Maritime Combat Systems, which included support for the [[Air Warfare Destroyer]] project. He has also chaired the Maritime Systems Group of [[The Technical Cooperation Program]] (TTCP).<ref name="DSTO"/>

{{As of|2015}}, Riley was back in Adelaide, as Chief of the Weapons and Combat Systems Division of DSTO.<ref name="Malthouse"/><ref name="DSTO"/> He retired in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realestate.com.au/news/exrooster-john-riley-hopes-auction-goes-nuclear/ |website=[[realestate.com.au]] |title=Ex-rooster John Riley hopes auction goes nuclear |date=22 August 2022 |access-date=29 October 2024 |first=Tom |last=Bowden |publisher=[[News Corp Australia]]}}</ref>

==Football==
Originally from [[Broadview, South Australia|Broadview]], Riley made his [[SANFL]] debut in 1977 and by 1982 was North Adelaide captain. In 1982, he also won the club's 'fairest and most brilliant' award and took part in South Australia's interstate fixtures.

He was lured to the VFL in 1984 when Footscray signed him and made his first appearance in the opening round of the [[1984 VFL season]], with eight disposals in a win over Richmond.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://afltables.com/afl/stats/players/J/John_Riley.html| title=John Riley| publisher=AFL Tables}}</ref> However, he had not been granted a clearance by North Adelaide, and the club was successful in getting a Supreme Court injunction to prevent him playing more games at Footscray.<ref>''The Age'', "Riley stays", 13 April 1984, p. 24</ref>

Riley finished the season with North Adelaide and remained with the club until 1990, amassing 250 games. After playing in their 1985 and 1986 Grand Final losses, Riley was on the half back flank when they won the 1987 premiership decider. He was later named at the same position in the North Adelaide 'Team of the Century'.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://australianfootball.com/players/player/john%2Briley/11904|title=John Riley – Player Bio| publisher=australianfootball.com}}</ref>
